text.p: Following are the main stories in Wednesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Twenty-eight leaders of the information technology industry have been appointed to the International Advisory Panel that Malaysia has formed to guide the development of its information technology backbone, the Multimedia Super Corridor.
-- Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad urged Malaysians living abroad to master the languages of the countries in which they reside. He said this while on a week-long visit to the U.S.
-- The Registrar of Companies is investigating five companies that have allegedly contravened the Companies Act by acting as non-governmental organisations.
-- Malaysian central bank, Bank Negara, is seen by rating agency Standard & Poor's as one of the best financial regulators in the region, the agency said in a report.

-- The Copyright Act is to be amended this year to protect against the theft of intellectual property and to boost investor confidence, said Domestic Trade and Consumer Affairs Minister Abu Hassan Omar on Tuesday. The changes will be made to cater for the advent of new multimedia services in the country.
